question_text: For a standard domestic First-Class Mail letter, what maximum weight does one First-Class Mail Forever stamp cover before extra-ounce postage is needed?
correct_answer: One Forever stamp covers a letter weighing up to 1 ounce.
incorrect_answer: One Forever stamp covers a letter weighing up to 2 ounces.
ground_truth_note: USPS states that First-Class Mail letters are priced starting at up to 1 ounce, with an additional charge for each extra ounce.

question_text: When requesting mail to be held for a temporary absence, what is the maximum number of consecutive days USPS will generally hold the mail?
correct_answer: USPS Hold Mail can generally be scheduled for up to 30 consecutive days.
incorrect_answer: USPS Hold Mail can generally be scheduled for up to 45 consecutive days.
ground_truth_note: USPS describes Hold Mail service as available for a minimum of 3 days and a maximum of 30 days.

question_text: For domestic USPS Priority Mail service, how much insurance is generally included at no additional charge?
correct_answer: Domestic Priority Mail generally includes up to $100 of insurance.
incorrect_answer: Domestic Priority Mail generally includes up to $50 of insurance.
ground_truth_note: USPS lists up to $100 of included insurance for most domestic Priority Mail shipments.

question_text: For most products bought directly from Apple in the United States, what is the standard return period after receiving the item?
correct_answer: Most eligible products can be returned within 14 calendar days after receipt.
incorrect_answer: Most eligible products can be returned within 30 calendar days after receipt.
ground_truth_note: Apple’s U.S. return policy states that eligible products generally may be returned within 14 calendar days after receipt.

question_text: Under the general carry-on liquids rule for U.S. airport screening, what is the maximum size allowed for each liquid, aerosol, gel, cream, or paste container?
correct_answer: Each container may be 3.4 ounces or 100 milliliters or smaller.
incorrect_answer: Each container may be 4.0 ounces or 120 milliliters or smaller.
ground_truth_note: TSA’s 3-1-1 liquids rule allows travel-size containers that are 3.4 ounces, or 100 milliliters, or less per item.

question_text: When substituting dried herbs for fresh herbs in a recipe, what general amount of dried herbs should be used?
correct_answer: Use about one-third as much dried herb as fresh herb.
incorrect_answer: Use about one-half as much dried herb as fresh herb.
source_citation: UNL Extension, Food preparation guidance on herb substitutions
ground_truth_note: The extension guidance gives the common conversion of 1 teaspoon dried herbs for 1 tablespoon fresh herbs, which is one-third as much.

question_text: In general at the federal level, what additional tax applies to an IRA distribution taken before age 59½ when no exception applies?
correct_answer: The distribution is generally subject to an additional 10% tax.
incorrect_answer: The distribution is generally subject to an additional 15% tax.
source_citation: IRS Publication 590-B, Distributions from Individual Retirement Arrangements
ground_truth_note: IRS Publication 590-B states that early IRA distributions before age 59½ are generally subject to a 10% additional tax unless an exception applies.

question_text: At the federal level, after receiving a COBRA election notice, how long does a qualified beneficiary generally have to elect COBRA continuation coverage?
correct_answer: A qualified beneficiary generally has 60 days to elect COBRA coverage.
incorrect_answer: A qualified beneficiary generally has 45 days to elect COBRA coverage.
ground_truth_note: The Department of Labor states that qualified beneficiaries have 60 days to decide whether to elect COBRA continuation coverage.

question_text: For a federal IRS notice of deficiency addressed to a person within the United States, how long does the person generally have to file a petition with the U.S. Tax Court?
correct_answer: The person generally has 90 days from the notice date to file.
incorrect_answer: The person generally has 120 days from the notice date to file.
source_citation: U.S. Tax Court, Starting a Case
ground_truth_note: The U.S. Tax Court explains that a deficiency petition generally must be filed within 90 days after the notice is mailed, or 150 days if addressed outside the United States.

question_text: Under the federal credit-card billing-error dispute process, by when must a consumer generally send a written dispute after the bill containing the error was sent?
correct_answer: The consumer generally must send the written dispute within 60 days.
incorrect_answer: The consumer generally must send the written dispute within 90 days.
ground_truth_note: The FTC explains that, to preserve billing-error rights under the Fair Credit Billing Act, the written dispute must reach the creditor within 60 days after the first bill with the error was sent.

question_text: At the federal level, who generally must register with the Selective Service System based on age and sex?
correct_answer: Male U.S. citizens and male immigrants generally must register from ages 18 through 25.
incorrect_answer: Male U.S. citizens and male immigrants generally must register from ages 18 through 30.
source_citation: Selective Service System, Who Needs to Register
ground_truth_note: Selective Service states that almost all male U.S. citizens and male immigrants who are 18 through 25 are required to register.

question_text: For someone first eligible for Medicare at age 65 and not automatically enrolled, when does the Initial Enrollment Period generally run for Medicare Part B?
correct_answer: It runs for seven months, from three months before through three months after the month the person turns 65.
incorrect_answer: It runs for seven months, from the month the person turns 65 through six months after that month.
source_citation: Medicare.gov, When does Medicare coverage start?
ground_truth_note: Medicare.gov describes the Initial Enrollment Period as starting 3 months before the month a person turns 65, including that month, and ending 3 months after that month.
